findings.description: No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects in this bucket are stored without enforced encryption at rest.

findings.issue_category: missing bucket ACL / public access controls
findings.description: No acl attribute or public access block is set, leaving the bucket to default settings and no explicit enforcement of private access, increasing risk of unintended public exposure.
Versioning is not enabled, which combined with force_destroy = true means data can be permanently and irrecoverably lost or tampered with without any recovery option.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for a bucket storing ledger export data, leaving sensitive financial data unencrypted at rest.
Versioning is not enabled for a financial ledger export bucket combined with force_destroy = true, risking permanent data loss or undetected tampering/overwrite of sensitive records.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is present, so model artifacts are stored without encryption at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is present, so operational runbook data (potentially containing sensitive operational/credential information) is stored unencrypted at rest.

The acl value 'lcatalogopts-delivery-write' is not a standard S3 canned ACL; if it resolves to a write-enabling ACL (e.g., log-delivery-write) it could allow unintended parties to write to the audit trail bucket, undermining the integrity of audit logs.

The object is uploaded to reports_archive bucket which has no server-side encryption configured, and no server_side_encryption or kms_key_id argument is set on the object itself, so this file is stored without encryption at rest.
force_destroy = true permits deletion of the bucket along with all its contents without safeguards, risking accidental or malicious permanent data loss.
